title: Daily mathematics — arXiv announcement batch 2026-11-23: 10 notable recent papers
global_caveat: arXiv provides no official trending chart. This ordering is inferred from sparse attention/citation signals; the signal file has 150 scored candidate entries against 301 archive records, so it is not an exhaustive popularity ranking.

sections.title: On the interplay between the anisotropy and the regularity of the coefficients in non autonomous problems
sections.abstract: The authors establish local Lipschitz regularity for minimizers of non-autonomous integral functionals under a balance between coefficient regularity and non-uniform ellipticity.
sections.claimed_result: The authors’ Theorem 1.2 claims local W^{1,∞} regularity, with an interior gradient estimate, for local minimizers satisfying structural assumptions (F1)–(F6).
sections.assumptions_and_setting: A bounded open Ω⊂Rⁿ, n≥2; radial Uhlenbeck-type integrands with general gradient growth, p>1, and coefficient/ellipticity conditions including an Orlicz–Sobolev regularity balance.
sections.unique_caveat: The conclusion is conditional on the detailed structural assumptions (F1)–(F6); it does not cover arbitrary non-autonomous integrands.

sections.title: Equivariant extension of $I_N$-finite tempered distributions on real flag varieties
sections.abstract: For a real reductive group, the paper proves that every $I_N$-finite tempered distribution on a $Q$-stable Nash open subset of $G/P$ extends to the whole flag variety.
sections.claimed_result: Theorem A states that restriction from the full real flag variety to a Q-stable Nash open subset is surjective on spaces of I_N-finite tempered distributions.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: G is a real linear reductive group; P and Q are parabolic subgroups; F is a Casselman–Wallach representation of the Levi of P, and the distributions are tempered sections of the induced homogeneous bundle.
sections.unique_caveat: The extension theorem requires Q-stability and I_N-finiteness; it is not a statement for arbitrary open subsets or unrestricted distributions.

sections.title: A proof of Cigler's quadratic recurrence for Hankel determinants of Motzkin path generating functions
sections.abstract: The paper proves Cigler’s conjectured quadratic recurrence for Hankel determinants built from weighted Motzkin-path generating polynomials, for every k≥0 and n≥2k+2.
sections.claimed_result: The author proves the stated recurrence for all k≥0 and n≥2k+2, and independently proves the companion determinant formula showing the determinants do not depend on c.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Motzkin paths stay nonnegative; level steps weigh c+x at height zero and c above it; D_{k,n} is the n×n Hankel determinant of the endpoint-count polynomials.
sections.unique_caveat: The recurrence has the explicit range n≥2k+2; the companion c-independence claim had also recently been proved by V. Jandhyala, according to the author.
sections.comment: 19 pages; an earlier version is on Zenodo, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.24369438

sections.title: Hankel determinants of Motzkin path generating functions and the Hirota-Miwa equation
sections.abstract: The paper relates Cigler’s Motzkin-path Hankel recurrence to the Hirota–Miwa equation and extends related identities to other moment functionals and symplectic-character determinants.
sections.claimed_result: The author gives a second derivation of Cigler’s recurrence as a reduction of Hirota–Miwa, extends it to moment functionals with specified eventual Chebyshev recurrence coefficients, and derives further determinant identities.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Weighted Motzkin-path moments and their Hankel determinants; the extension assumes a moment functional whose recurrence coefficients match the Chebyshev regime above a height N.
sections.unique_caveat: The generalized recurrence depends on the stated moment-functional recurrence condition; it is not asserted for arbitrary sequences of moments.
sections.comment: 40 pages; ancillary files contain computer checks

sections.title: Planar cut-and-project sets with interval windows are bi-Lipschitz equivalent to lattices
sections.abstract: Every planar cut-and-project set in R³ with a segment window, or a finite union of interval windows, is proved bi-Lipschitz equivalent to Z² without a Diophantine condition on the plane.
sections.claimed_result: The author proves the lattice equivalence for segment and finite-union-of-interval windows, and contrasts it with a compact countable-boundary window example that is not lattice-equivalent.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: A plane V⊂R³ not spanned by integer vectors, translated by x, with a transverse line-segment window; the result also covers finite unions of intervals.
sections.unique_caveat: The positive result is shape-specific: the paper’s own comparison example shows that compact windows with countable boundary can fail lattice equivalence.

sections.title: The weighted fundamental lemma for non-split groups
sections.abstract: The paper proves the Lie-algebra Weighted Fundamental Lemma for general quasi-split unramified groups via Higgs-bundle geometry, global cohomology, and a local-to-global argument.
sections.claimed_result: The author claims the Weighted Fundamental Lemma for Lie algebras and a deduction of Waldspurger’s nonstandard version, with consequences for stabilization of the twisted Arthur–Selberg trace formula.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Quasi-split unramified reductive groups; the properness result for the stack of ξ-stable Higgs bundles assumes anisotropic center, and the stated twisted consequence is in good characteristic.
sections.unique_caveat: The announced downstream classification consequences are conditional on the paper’s characteristic and group hypotheses; the 190-page preprint has not been independently proof-checked here.

sections.title: Source Conditions and Sharp Transition Asymptotics for the Factorization Method with Far-Field Data
sections.abstract: For inverse acoustic scattering, the authors derive sharp regularization-bias and spectral-transition asymptotics for disc and more general impedance obstacles, including explicit interior, boundary, and exterior behavior.
sections.claimed_result: The authors derive Lambert-W transition asymptotics, quantitative threshold/boundary-location estimates, and a sharp spectral law for a class of analytic obstacles.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Factorization-method reconstruction from far-field data for impedance obstacles; the general analytic normal-form result assumes a simply connected obstacle, analytic boundary, positive analytic impedance, and the conformal center inside.
sections.unique_caveat: The sharp analytic normal-form result is proved only for a single boundary component; the general-obstacle estimates are broader but weaker.

sections.title: Uniqueness of $L_{p}$ Minkowski Problem in the supercritical range near the affine exponent
sections.abstract: For the isotropic $L_p$-Minkowski problem, the paper proves uniqueness in a dimension-dependent interval immediately below the affine-invariant exponent p=−n−1.
sections.claimed_result: The author establishes uniform C⁰ bounds and a spectral estimate, then proves uniqueness for p∈(−n−1−δ_n,−n−1) with δ_n>0.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The isotropic L_p-Minkowski equation in dimension n, in the supercritical regime near the affine exponent p=−n−1.
sections.unique_caveat: The result covers only a dimension-dependent neighborhood below p=−n−1; it does not settle uniqueness throughout the full supercritical range.

sections.title: The Ritt problem is decidable
sections.abstract: The authors give an affirmative solution to the Ritt decidability problem and derive equivalent decision procedures for several foundational differential-algebra tasks.
sections.claimed_result: Theorem 1.1 claims decidability of primality and prime decomposition for finitely generated radical differential ideals, finite generation from characteristic sets, and containment of prime differential ideals.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Computable ordinary differential fields of characteristic zero with a splitting algorithm; the paper reduces the decision tasks to deciding containment of prime differential ideals.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors say the current algorithm is impractical and gives no effective runtime/sequence-length bounds; they disclose that the argument was generated using an AI model, making expert review especially important.

sections.title: On the Laugesen--Siudeja Conjecture: A Sharp Lower Bound and Failure of the Upper Bound
sections.abstract: For every bounded convex planar domain, the paper proves the sharp lower bound λ₁A³/I>9π²/2 and gives a trapezoidal counterexample to the conjectured upper bound.
sections.claimed_result: The author proves the lower bound, approached by thin isosceles triangles, and exhibits an isosceles trapezoid with λ₁A³/I>12π², disproving the proposed upper bound.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The first Dirichlet eigenvalue λ₁, area A, and centroidal polar moment of inertia I for bounded convex domains in the plane.
sections.unique_caveat: The conclusion is planar and assumes convexity; the counterexample disproves the proposed upper bound but does not characterize all possible upper estimates.
